wording: In a speciation continuum of hybridizing races and incipient species of Heliconius erato-clade butterflies, genomic divergence increases with ecological and reproductive isolation, both at the red colour-pattern locus and at genomic regions unlinked to colour pattern.
counterevidence_limits: 2.2 Mb of the H. erato genome only; a handful of population pairs; continuum stages are proxies for speciation stages, not a time series.
operationalization: Divergence = genomic differentiation between populations along a speciation continuum
verification_phrases: P01|genomic divergence increases with ecological and reproductive isolation

wording: The same study infers that divergence may accumulate early in the speciation process and that limited gene flow cannot account for the high divergence between the incipient species H. erato and H. himera.
counterevidence_limits: Inference from one incipient-species pair; alternative histories (e.g. older isolation) are not excluded by the data shown.
operationalization: Divergence with gene flow (divergence proceeding despite exchange)
verification_phrases: P01|divergence may accumulate early in the speciation process

wording: In a neutral two-deme Wright-Fisher model (N = 100, 400 loci), drift alone raised Fst to 0.385 after 200 generations (heterozygosity decay matched theory within 5%), whereas symmetric migration with Nm = 1 held Fst at 0.056: gene flow strongly restrains neutral divergence.
counterevidence_limits: Toy neutral model; the H1 threshold was moved from 0.5 to 0.25 after a pre-spec smoke test (disclosed in the SPEC). Selection, which drives the colour-locus divergence in P01, is absent.
